title: Rules of Procedure: Terms, Voting and the Council
summary: The monthly political cycle, voting thresholds, sealed tallies, proxies, scheduling guarantees, Council delays and vetoes, and the path from motion to enforceable claim.

sections.heading: One month, ten years
paragraphs: One real month is one term, representing ten years in the setting. The game is asynchronous; every action is recorded with both a real deadline and a simulated effective date. Political debate occurs through the official website and Discord; the public ledger, rather than any single chat thread, is authoritative.

table.caption: The four weeks of a term
rows: Election results; seating the Assembly; Speaker election and Bureau formation; nominations for Commissioner and Commission on Long-Term Inquiry.
Bill and prohibition filings; caucus bargaining; public briefs and petitions; the Arbiter accepts eligible queries.
Votes open for 72 hours with totals sealed. The Council then receives a 48-hour window to delay or exercise a protected veto.
First 48 hours for delay overrides; resources and goal accounting; simulated events, public scorecard and noisy polls; next election campaign.

sections.heading: Voting thresholds
paragraphs: Ordinary passage is a simple majority of seats voting, excluding abstentions. Bloc votes are all-or-nothing.

table.caption: Thresholds
rows: Simple majority of seats voting (abstentions excluded)
Override of a Council or Commissioner delay
Ninety per cent of seats voting
Two-thirds, plus consent of the rest-of-world Council seat
Removal of a Tribunal member for misconduct

sections.heading: Sealed tallies and publication
paragraphs: Votes remain sealed throughout their 72-hour window, including from the Speaker and Bureau. When the window closes, the complete roll call is published: each bloc's position and seat weight, abstentions, proxies, the threshold and the final seat-weighted result.

sections.heading: Blocs, proxies and inactivity
list: Each player ordinarily controls one indivisible party bloc. A player may never control more than sixty seats.
A player may appoint a party proxy; the designation must be filed before the vote opens. Otherwise a non-voting bloc abstains.
A bloc whose player does not vote through a full term passes to the next member on the party's list in the next term.
While serving, the Speaker transfers control of their voting bloc to the party's floor leader. Tribunal members and the Commissioner relinquish their blocs; Commission members keep theirs.

sections.heading: Scheduling guarantee
paragraphs: A measure filed on time must not be suppressed by agenda inaction. Anything the Bureau has failed to schedule by the end of Week 2 automatically reaches the Week 3 floor.

sections.heading: Council delays and vetoes
paragraphs: If an ordinary measure passes, the Council may delay it once with at least four votes. A delay is a suspensive power, not a veto; it can be overridden by a two-thirds Assembly vote in Week 4. One override also suffices if the Commissioner for Future Generations delays the same measure.

The Council's entrenched vetoes apply only to the four protected matters set out in [[DOC-COUNCIL|Council Seats and Protected Matters]]. The Arbiter determines whether a measure falls within the list, subject to Tribunal review.

sections.heading: Filing a motion for an allocation
paragraphs: A member seeking an ordinary Assembly allocation must write a motion specifying the requested resource amount or share, the channel, the intended use, the geographic reach, the implementing actor, and conditions for success or failure.

After the Week 3 vote and any Council action or override, the enacted decision becomes an entry in the public resource ledger following legal review. The following term reports its administrative, political and — where travel times permit — physical consequences. Passing a bill does not teleport probes to their destinations.

sections.heading: Actions not yet authorised
paragraphs: Resolutions without binding legal effect and general information-request powers are not yet authorised as separate gameplay actions. They are a possible future procedural amendment, not part of the founding rules.
